standard_prerequisites: The unit type with its induction principle: every element is definitionally the canonical element.
Equivalences via quasi-inverse: a function with a two-sided inverse up to identification.
The induction principle for identity types (path induction).
core_obligations: Construct a function from x = y to the unit type and a function from the unit type to x = y.
Prove that the two functions are quasi-inverse, using induction on the unit type at the last possible moment.
Conclude that x = y is equivalent to the unit type for all x, y in the unit type.
proof_roadmap: Define the first function by sending every path to the canonical element of the unit type.

For the reverse function, induct on x and y only at the last moment: work with general x and y as long as possible, then use unit induction to reduce them to the canonical element, where reflexivity inhabits the path type; the resulting function is constant.
Verify the first composite: an element of the unit type is sent to itself by definition under the current assumptions.
Verify the second composite: given p in x = y, induct on p to reduce to reflexivity, then induct on the endpoint; the composite sends p to reflexivity, which is p under the assumptions.
difficulty_reason: The induction order is the whole content: naive unit induction first would make the path induction impossible; the author's last-moment-reduction discipline must be followed exactly.
